record.paper_title: Open Questions in Cosmic-Ray Research at Ultrahigh Energies
record.original_question: What fluxes of cosmogenic neutrinos and gamma rays, produced when ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays interact with extragalactic background photons during propagation, should be expected across the allowed source-composition, maximum-energy, source-evolution, magnetic-field, and hadronic-model parameter space, and what would those neutral secondary messengers reveal about the sources of ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays?

evidence.quote: Neutral secondaries including neutrinos and photons are expected to be produced when UHECRs interact with extragalactic background photons during intergalactic propagation.
Their ﬂux mainly depends on the chemical composition, maximum energy of UHECRs, and the source evolution model (e.g., [61, 62]; see [63, 64] for secondaries from heavy nuclei).
What is the ﬂux of secondary messengers — neutrinos, gamma rays — associated with UHECRs, and what can we infer from them about UHECR sources?

Action item 7: Generate predictions of the cosmogenic neutrino ﬂux by scanning across all of the available parameter space of UHECR model parameters — including uncertainties in magnetic ﬁelds and hadronic interaction models — in order to fully characterize the uncertainties.

artifact.category_tag: Cosmogenic neutrino and gamma-ray fluxes from UHECR propagation
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of fully characterizing cosmogenic neutrino and gamma-ray fluxes across the allowed UHECR parameter space remains an active open research direction. Recent (2024–2025) literature continues to produce new flux predictions and to debate the compatibility of events such as KM3NeT's KM3-230213A with cosmogenic origins, indicating that comprehensive parameter-space scans and source inferences are still being refined rather than settled.

status_evidence.title: Ultrahigh energy cosmic rays and neutrino flux models (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent reviews discuss model-independent benchmarks and model-dependent neutrino flux predictions tied to UHECRs.
status_evidence.claim: Cosmogenic neutrino flux predictions and their UHECR-parameter dependence remain an active modeling problem.

status_evidence.title: Ultra-high energy event KM3-230213A as a cosmogenic neutrino in light of minimal UHECR flux models (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Examines whether KM3NeT's 220 PeV event is cosmogenic, contingent on UHECR composition and source-evolution assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Inferring UHECR sources from cosmogenic neutrinos is still being actively investigated and debated.

status_evidence.title: Can KM3-230213A be compatible with a cosmogenic origin? (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies show subdominant proton fractions and high-redshift integration can enhance cosmogenic flux to match observations.
status_evidence.claim: Allowed parameter space and corresponding flux envelopes are still being mapped.
